name: Tetrahydrocurcuminoids (applied to skin)
short: Case report: contact allergy to tetrahydrocurcumin. Turmeric review: allergy case reports (route unstated). Patch test, 36 women: less irritation than positive control; allergy testing not reported.
text: On the skin, a case report (published without an abstract) describes contact allergy to tetrahydrocurcumin; a review of turmeric (these compounds are produced chemically from curcuminoids extracted from turmeric rhizomes) notes that turmeric is commonly applied to the skin in South India and that its allergenic potential is mentioned in various case reports and studies, without saying by which route. In a single closed patch test in 36 female volunteers, 12 test materials, including a tetrahydrocurcuminoid extract and a commercial cream, caused significantly less skin irritation than the positive control, and the authors concluded the products were not likely to irritate skin under normal use; the abstract does not report allergy testing. By mouth, which is a different route, an open-label pilot trial in 60 people with canker sores or gingivitis using chewable tablets for 21 days reported no adverse effects, and a European Food Safety Authority panel, assessing the compounds as a food supplement on the basis of a 90-day oral toxicity study and a reproduction and developmental toxicity screening test, found no genotoxicity concerns and judged them safe for the target population (adults, excluding pregnant and breastfeeding women) at a level lower than the applicant proposed. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
